text: Ethereum's Dencun upgrade, which activated in March 2024, introduced proto-danksharding via EIP-4844 and dramatically lowered Layer-2 transaction costs. Optimism and Arbitrum saw fees fall by over 90% in the first week. The upgrade also introduced blob-carrying transactions, a new transaction type that stores data off the main EVM state in a separate data-availability layer, pruned after roughly 18 days. This is a stepping stone toward full danksharding.

Remote work adoption accelerated during the 2020 pandemic and has since stabilized at a higher baseline than before. Most knowledge-worker companies adopted hybrid models with 2-3 days in office. Fully remote startups grew in number but face retention challenges. Office vacancy rates in major US cities remain elevated, with San Francisco seeing 35% vacancy in late 2024. Companies are increasingly tying promotions to in-office presence.

Abstract: We present a novel approach to zero-knowledge rollup proving that reduces proof generation time by 40% through parallelized SNARK construction. Our benchmarks on a 128-core server show sustained throughput of 2,800 TPS for the Polygon zkEVM circuit. We also introduce a new polynomial commitment scheme that halves on-chain verification gas cost. Code and benchmarks are available on GitHub.

Product spec: User authentication v2. Goal: migrate from session-cookie auth to signed JWT with rotating refresh tokens. Refresh tokens rotate every 24h; access tokens expire after 15 minutes. Tokens signed with RS256 (public key published at /.well-known/jwks.json). Mobile apps must handle 401 + refresh flow transparently. Migration rollout: 1% canary on Dec 1, 50% Dec 8, 100% Dec 15.
